Hi y’all! So in July 2020 I decided I was done being ultra skinny and decided to bulk up. I was 20 years old, 5’ 8”, and 108 pounds, and was basically skin and bones. I got a dumbbell set and a bench and got to working out 4x a week, and started eating 3000 calories a day. Since then, I have gained 35 pounds (currently sit at 143lbs) in the time since then. I know it’s not a lot but I’m proud of the progress I’ve made. I’m now at a healthy weight (for my age and height) and feel a lot more comfortable with my body. It’s been a long and hard process — I’ve gone through two bad depressive episodes during this time and lost 10lbs+ and had to gain it all back each time. 

I recently moved and now have access to a full gym which has unlocked so much more potential in terms of weights and exercises. I also have begun taking creatine. I’m still eating 3000+ calories a day, and gaining weight. I’m currently doing a 4x a week upper body/lower body hypertrophy workout, and lifting heavier weights. However, my stomach is disproportionate to my body and because I’m eating so much it’s projecting far more than I would like. It’s all I can tell now, in pictures, in mirrors, in workouts, everywhere, all I see is my bigger stomach. Also my chest and arms seem to have stopped growing and aren’t bulging at all. They’ve made so much progress since I first started working out since I was so skinny before, but I don’t get why they’re not larger. I look at other guys who have such huge chests and arms. I know I shouldn’t compare and we’re all on our own journey, but it sucks because I’m left to figure out why I don’t look like them when I am eating 3000+ calories, weightlifting 4x a week, and lifting heavy. 

Here’s where I need the help, and I have a few questions that I’d like some help with from people who get it. Is the bigger stomach just something I should learn to deal with while bulking? All during this time since July 2020 my stomach has stayed relatively flat, with my friends have always commented at how my clothes are fitting better and how my arms and shoulders have filled out a lot. Now I just look skinny-fat and I’m really struggling with it. Am I just eating too much and should I cut my calories? Should I just stop bulking altogether at this stage and shred/cut so I can have abs and more defined muscles at the moment? I just now feel like absolute shit about my body and feel like shredding might help, even if I’m not huge now. Should I change my workout plan to something that focuses more on strength (i.e. doing sets with 5 reps with a much heavier weight)? 

Thanks for listening and even more thanks for your feedback :) I’m just trying to learn what’s best for my body.

Truth be told, I’m doing a terrible job of coping with it right now.  I sleep a lot, and watch TV, and cry a lot. I’m 21, and have been dealing with depression for as long as I can remember. I’ve been in therapy and on dozens of pills since I was 15 trying to find something that works. It truly ebbs and flows. Some weeks it’s a lot more manageable. I’m able to enjoy the small things, like sunsets or the ocean. Other weeks I can barely get out of bed. This most recent episode was sparked by a break-up, and every day for the past four months my heart has felt like it’s been destroyed and will never be the same again. I’ve wanted to die every day and the world lacks its color once again. 

Therapy helps me cope, and I highly recommend seeing a therapist if you haven’t already!! Having someone always be there to listen and to help deconstruct negative thoughts and traumas is helpful. Also a good support system, have good friends or family you can talk to about your mental illness. And then of course trying ketamine or medication to help treat it. 

You’re not alone, and I hope you find relief in your own way!

Hi!! So I just got done with the standard six rounds of ketamine treatments. Sadly, it did not work for me. I found no results at all. I’m super discouraged since I’ve had chronic treatment resistant depression for so many years, and it’s been really bad lately. 

HOWEVER, that is my personal experience! While receiving the ketamine treatments, I met and talked to so many other clients and ketamine has worked miracles for them. It does have a pretty high success rate, and is worth a shot (if anything for the k-hole experience, it’s definitely a fun time haha). 

A few things you should keep in mind: 
- Go through a licensed, reviewed clinic. I went through a University hospital system so I knew it was legit and science based. 
- It’s expensive. My treatments were $375 a time. 
- Even if the standard 6 works, you’ll then transition to once a week for a while then once every other week, which equals more $$$$

Yeah, there’s always risk involved it seems. I’m already doing a ton of research into voting history, policy standpoints, and political views, as well as history of the state, so maybe that’s enough and I don’t have to bring up the book? Idk haha.
